Change c0194. Location: 1818 Vol. II, Ch. I; 1831 Ch. IX.

Context before (unchanged): I would have made a pilgrimage to the highest peak of the Andes, could I, when there, have precipitated him to their base.

1818 text: I wished to see him again, that I might wreak the utmost extent of anger on his head, and avenge the deaths of William and Justine.

1831 text: I wished to see him again, that I might wreak the utmost extent of abhorrence on his head, and avenge the deaths of William and Justine.

Diff: I wished to see him again, that I might wreak the utmost extent of [-anger-] {+abhorrence+} on his head, and avenge the deaths of William and Justine.

Context after (unchanged): Our house was the house of mourning.

result.rationale: Replacing 'anger' with 'abhorrence' shifts Victor's emotional stance from hot, personal rage to a moral revulsion toward the creature, making his vengeful desire read as judgment rather than passion; the change is one word but reframes his motive.
